sections.title: Dashboard, hosts, and discovery
rows: One UI for services across the Pi, mini PC, and laptop.
Responsive phone layout plus installable PWA, home-screen icons and a versioned offline app shell. Service data and controls require the controller.
Cards with state and controls; filter by host, tag, and state.
Service cards with host, tag and state filters, plus full-text search.
Represent an application as one service containing its containers, units, processes, files, and metadata.

Applications link same-host runtime components under one card while preserving every notebook, file policy and control permission; installation, backup-plan and recovery documentation are editable and exported.
Controller on the Pi; local agents discover and operate services on each managed Linux host.
Controller-to-agent HTTP transport and per-host registration are implemented; deployment is still to verify.
Online, stale, and offline states based on agent heartbeats.

Opt-in 15-second persistent authenticated heartbeats with mutual HMAC proof, sequence-bound signed frames, durable handshake replay refusal, 45-second stale/150-second offline limits and immediate disconnect refusal; polling supports older agents.
Handle the intermittently connected laptop; reject offline commands explicitly instead of silently queuing them.
Offline/unverified host controls are refused; last inventory remains visible.
Discover standalone containers, ports, mounts, and runtime details.
Standalone containers, published ports, mounts, image, state and runtime details are discovered.
Recognize Compose projects from labels and identify their components and paths.
Project labels, working directories and grouped components are discovered.
Discover system services and their units.
Loaded units and enabled/linked unloaded units are discovered, including enabled-state metadata.
Opt-in selected pm2 metadata from an existing agent-owned daemon and configured PM2_HOME; environment values are omitted and discovery refuses to bootstrap an absent daemon.
Suggest services from listening sockets not owned by another recognized runtime.
Prefill names, icons, and URLs for known applications such as Minecraft, Ollama, and Portainer.
Deterministic Minecraft/Ollama/Kuma/Portainer/Vaultwarden/Tailscale/Samba fingerprints prefill identity and suitable access URLs.
Hide routine system units by default, with an option to reveal them.
Routine OS units are hidden by default; discovery can reveal them without falsely marking hidden units missing.
Group related components using Compose projects, wrapper units, or shared working directories.
Compose grouping plus explicit same-host cross-runtime relationships, exact native working-directory suggestions, dependency-order group controls and cycle/nesting/duplicate-control checks.
Correct service grouping through the UI.
Notebook checkboxes link/unlink application components without deleting or merging their notes; child notebooks remain accessible and relationships round-trip in manifests/Markdown.
Review new, changed, and gone services; accept or reject candidates.
Persistent new/changed/gone/unchanged review with field diffs, explicit selection and recorded unaccepted candidates. Missing notebooks are preserved.
Scan on demand and periodically, defaulting to every six hours.
On-demand discovery and six-hour live-host discovery reviews, alongside periodic observations.

sections.title: Service control, monitoring, and power
rows: One-click runtime-specific control for Docker, Compose, systemd, pm2, and configured raw processes.

Docker/Compose/systemd, verified numeric pm2 instances and fixed Linux/macOS process profiles; PID/time/executable/profile checks, uncertain-outcome refusal and no force-kill. macOS launchd and Windows service controls remain read-only.
Enable/disable startup behavior for systemd and Compose through their respective mechanisms.
Select several services and perform an action together.
Selected services execute sequentially with confirmation and individual audit outcomes.
Offer to start dependencies; warn before stopping a service another running service needs.
Explicit dependency-first startup, cycle/reference validation, full-plan preflight, verified prerequisite state and dependent-stop warnings.
Show running, stopped, restarting, failed, or unknown state.
Known states refresh through polling and after controls; offline services become unobserved.
HTTP(S), TCP, and custom-command checks; default interval of 60 seconds.
HTTP(S)/TCP/ICMP plus agent-owned fixed custom-check profiles, configurable intervals/timeouts, and synthetic demo checks; arbitrary caller commands are refused.
Uptime percentages for 24 hours, seven days, and 30 days.
Time-weighted observed uptime for 24h/7d/30d, with bounded sample carry-forward and explicit unknown time/coverage.
Store latency, outages, and recent incident history.
Latency history, persistent outage/recovery incidents, observed durations, cause editing and linked investigation notes.
CPU usage, memory usage, restart count, and uptime since last start.

Docker/Compose, systemd cgroup/main-process and Windows service-process CPU/memory snapshots, observed scopes, restart/start metadata, and a consistent sampling opt-out. Unknown values stay unknown; live adapters remain deployment validation.
Notify about service failures, offline hosts, and repeated restarts.
Health failure/recovery, offline-host, repeated-restart and sustained host-threshold events feed an opt-in masked outbox with deduplication, bounded retries and simulated demo delivery.
Deliver alerts through ntfy or Telegram, with the channel chosen in settings.
ntfy/Telegram settings, environment-token references, save/test actions and delivery status; disabled by default. Real transports are mocked in tests; demo delivery is simulated.
Optional import of existing monitors, with the stated intent of retaining history.
Embed Kuma views or pull its data instead of building equivalent monitoring.
Ping/HTTP monitoring was proposed in the earlier dashboard discussion; the spec lists HTTP/TCP/custom checks.
HTTP(S), TCP and ICMP checks; ping arguments are fixed and targets validated. Demo probes remain simulated.
Send Wake-on-LAN packets from the Pi for configured hosts.

Fixed locally configured MAC/private IPv4/UDP7-or-9 profiles, confirmed fingerprint-bound dispatch, host-operation reservation, persistent cooldown and audits. Demo and test sockets never send a real packet; dispatch does not imply observed wake. Hardware/network support remains unverified.
Sleep or shut down a host, warning about its running services.

Reviewed host impact, signed fixed Linux/macOS/Windows suspend and shutdown adapters, ordinary-account approval, durable uncertain holds and inspection acknowledgements are implemented and mocked. macOS shutdown requires an explicitly approved current GUI domain. Native execution/permissions remain owner-deferred platform evidence; no real power command was executed.

Opt-in individual and grouped application start/stop schedules with explicit component consent, IANA timezone previews, DST gap/fold handling, durable once-only decisions, fresh dependency/revision guards and no offline replay. Demo never dispatches automatically.
Stop after a configured period without port connections; Minecraft’s example uses no players.

Standalone and linked-application auto-stop require continuous explicit activity signals for the application and every linked component, with up to eight component profiles. Unknown/active signals, revised components, offline hosts, external dependents and missing permissions inhibit stops. Group reservation, dependency order and observed stopped states protect manual wake; no CPU-only inactivity inference.
Start an automatically stopped service again from the UI.
Verified automatic stops mark standalone or entire linked applications asleep. Normal confirmed dependency-ordered startup clears sleep after verified running states.
Distinguish scheduled sleep from a manual stop.

Last controller start/stop/restart requests retain manual, idle or schedule origin, timestamp, outcome and observed-result flag. Unrecorded stops remain unknown; an accepted command is not proof of state or of later external changes.

sections.title: Service documentation and installation memory
rows: A single page combining identity, runtime, access, files, credentials, installation, backups, dependencies, and history.

Identity, runtime/components/resources, access, files/config history, credential pointers, dependencies, health, owner installation/backup/recovery documentation and history appear in one notebook. Plans are not proof of executed backups; recorder/backup engines are separate roadmap items.
Service name, icon, tags, description, and host association.
Name, icon, tags, description and host association are editable; moving a card clears its previous runtime access.
URLs, ports and protocols are stored, displayed and exported.
Working directory, configuration, data directories, volumes, and log locations.
Typed working/configuration/data/volume/log locations, discovery metadata and editable notebook fields; documentation does not grant filesystem permission.
Show Compose/unit configuration, restart policy, and boot behavior.
Runtime/resources page shows start/restart/boot policy metadata and rooted, masked Compose/unit document previews. Boot editing remains separate.
Show what a service needs and what depends on it.
Required services and reverse dependencies are displayed and editable.
Markdown editor, revision checks, previous notes and unsaved-draft protection are implemented.
Populate cards from discovery and keep observed fields current.
Observed state, capabilities, runtime details and discovered metadata refresh; owner edits/manual definitions remain protected.
Mark configuration or metadata as changed since the last review.
Cards show field-level drift against the last reviewed discovery snapshot; accepted reviews reset the baseline.
Present configuration changes, incidents, and control actions together.
Configuration changes, incidents and control actions are presented together with prior owner notes, installation/recovery documentation revisions and linked investigation records.
Search service cards by name, port, path, and documentation.
Names, descriptions, notes, tags, runtimes, hosts, paths and ports are searchable.
Export one service or the entire lab’s documentation.
Individual notes and a complete linked Markdown collection can be downloaded.
Portable lab.yaml plus a Markdown docs/ folder.
lab.yaml and docs export; reviewed, validated, repeatable import.
Record a named installation session’s terminal commands and output.
Named opt-in terminal sessions record bounded, best-effort masked input/output; metadata-only auditing by default. Demo is synthetic and a transcript does not prove installation success.
Store recordings using asciinema v2 cast format.
Opt-in recordings persist as private asciinema v2 cast artifacts with relative timing and output/resize events; authenticated scoped export omits input events.
Compare packages, systemd units, Docker resources, ports, and watched files.

Opt-in installation sessions compare bounded native package/app, service/unit, container, Docker image/network/volume, listening-port and approved file-hash metadata. Incomplete/different scopes do not imply removals; capture failure remains an explicit evidence gap. Native providers are mocked.
Watch standard locations and user-added directories for installation changes.

Locally approved per-reference watch directories must stay inside approved service file roots. Five-root, depth/time/file/byte budgets, symlink/junction/hardlink refusal and metadata-only UTF-8 hashes protect Linux/macOS/Windows capture; large/binary/secret files remain excluded.
Ignore noisy cache/log/temp changes and allow pruning before saving.

Noisy cache/log/temp paths are excluded during file capture; owners can omit commands or changes from a revision-checked installation review before saving/exporting instructions. Original masked evidence is retained; cleanup never deletes it.
Turn recording and snapshot differences into ordered instructions for user review.

Ordered captured-command and snapshot-change drafts, editable owner instructions, explicit review state and scoped Markdown export. Evidence/reconstructed/demo labels and gaps persist; nothing runs automatically and reproducibility is not claimed.
Import Bash, Zsh, and Fish history for services installed previously.

Explicit bounded pasted Bash, Zsh extended-history and Fish history-file excerpts import only secret-free commands matching the selected service. Raw/unrelated history is discarded; no history files are fetched automatically.
Match historical commands using service names, paths, images, and ports.

Service names/IDs, approved paths, images and numeric ports select candidate historical commands in source order; suspected credentials are omitted. Matching is heuristic and every inferred command remains unverified.
Clearly mark inferred installation instructions as reconstructed and unverified.

Imported histories, their review views, AI context and exported instructions are marked reconstructed/unverified. Demo evidence remains separately synthetic; owner approval never changes reproducibility to verified.

sections.title: Files, configuration history, logs, and terminal
rows: Browse files associated with each service.
Read-only directory navigation and UTF-8 previews within an approved agent root.
Edit text configuration with syntax highlighting for YAML, JSON, TOML, INI, .env, and shell files.

Approved Linux editing/history/restore plus Windows owner/DACL checks and ReplaceFileW recovery, and macOS ACL/xattr-preserving metadata copy are implemented with mocked tests. Actual native replacement/permissions behavior remains unverified; secret files stay excluded.
Explicit “open host root” toggle beyond service paths.
Planned text; conflicts with the stricter security section
Files over 2 MB become read-only; binaries are download-only.
Read-only previews of the first 2 MB of large text files; binary download-only view. Downloads are bounded to 2 MB and apply secret-file exclusions.
Commit UI saves into a per-service Git repository with a message.

Controller-owned per-service Git baseline/prospective snapshots precede remote writes; validated outcomes, host-operation reservations and unknown crash recovery protect history. Git is required on the controller.
Periodically capture changes made outside the dashboard.

Opt-in approved configuration capture detects baseline/changes, excludes secret/large/binary files, honors intervals, caps five files/service and three service attempts/live poll, and preserves notebook fields.
Scoped comparison between verified tracked versions, bounded unified diffs, preserved whitespace and a frontend Before/After selector.
Revert to a previous version with one click.
Review a scoped verified version and restore with current etag protection; records a new version and never restarts the service automatically.
Optional YAML/JSON validation and Compose configuration checks.
UTF-8/size/secret and YAML/JSON/TOML syntax checks; optional fixed agent argv validates a temporary candidate before atomic replacement. Failed validation preserves the original.
Exclude .env and other detected secret-bearing files from history by default.
Secret filenames and conservatively detected secret content are excluded from managed editing/history/capture; plain environment references are accepted. Detection is not exhaustive.
Stream Docker/Compose, systemd journal, pm2, or configured file logs.

Authenticated bounded Docker/Compose/journal/pm2 followers and approved file-log tailing, snapshot downloads, filtering/error navigation, pause/disconnect cleanup, rotation handling and per-agent/controller follower limits.
Filter, pause, search, and jump to errors.
Filter/search, refresh pause, highlighted warning/error lines and next-error navigation.
Download the last selected number of lines.
Authenticated snapshot downloads with a selectable 100/300/1000/5000-line limit and masking.
Open a real browser terminal in the service’s working directory.

Browser xterm with fixed locally approved argv/cwd profiles, POSIX PTY and optional Windows ConPTY adapters. Live execution requires signed transport and ordinary account checks; native target behavior remains unverified.
Explicit confirmation, non-root session user, 15-minute idle timeout, and optional reauthentication.

Explicit host/account/cwd confirmation, changed-profile refusal, owner-bound one-use tickets, optional recent login, host reservations, idle/absolute limits and disconnect cleanup. Cwd is not a filesystem sandbox.
Record session start/end and host; record content only when installation recording is enabled.
Session start/end, host/service/profile and outcome are durable metadata; terminal content is stored only with explicit installation recording. Transcript/cast exports are scoped and audited.
Cap simultaneous terminals and log streams to limit memory pressure.
Per-agent/controller terminal and log follower limits, bounded input/output/recordings, idle/absolute expiry, frame-rate caps and missing-poll cleanup.

sections.title: AI and credential handling
rows: Use the user’s Ollama instance; configure endpoint, model, timeout, and context limits.
Saved enable/endpoint/model/timeout/context settings, model availability checks and explicit-request Ollama explanations.
Explain what happened, likely cause, suggested fix, and confidence.
Ollama advice is generated on explicit request; real model accuracy is not verified.
Use recent or selected logs, service metadata, configuration changes, and incidents.

Bounded logs, metadata, discovery changes, incidents, audit history and scoped verified Git configuration diffs; unknown/prepared/other-service versions are excluded. Model requests remain explicit and advice-only.
Save AI responses as incident notes in service history.
AI responses save as dedicated incident notes in service history, or can be reviewed in an owner-note draft.
Draft editable service descriptions from configuration and application fingerprints.

Explicit-request local-model description drafts from stored observed metadata and up to two verified configuration-history files, with masking and credential refusal. Editable UI drafts require an explicit use action and notebook save; demo never contacts a model.
Convert recorded or historical commands into readable setup instructions.

Explicit-request advice-only model drafts use the saved reviewed installation evidence/exclusions. Returned instructions require owner review and a separate save; no commands run and model accuracy remains unverified.
Disable explanation actions with a reason when Ollama is unreachable.
Model-catalogue probes, clear disabled reasons, periodic rechecks while logs are open and retry after failed explanations.
Display suggested commands without executing them automatically.
Model output is displayed; commands are never executed automatically.
Store labels, optional usernames, Vaultwarden links/IDs, and non-secret location hints.
Labels, usernames, item links/IDs and hints are stored and exported; no password field.
Open vault links and copy usernames.
Scan during discovery and file saves for likely embedded credentials.

Best-effort fixed-category checks on discovery metadata, Docker environment assignments, locally approved exact configuration files and rejected configuration drafts. File roots, 20-file/64-KB/256-KB budgets and link/binary exclusions apply; secret filenames are flagged without reading contents. Findings contain no values, excerpts or value hashes. No root crawl; incomplete scope is explicit.
Flag apparently unvaulted secrets and let the owner link them to a vault item.

Persistent per-service findings show apparently unlinked credentials and let the owner save validated vault item links/IDs with finding revisions and audits. Linking never verifies item existence, secret removal or file safety; no vault login or credential export occurs.
Mask likely passwords, tokens, keys, headers, and high-entropy values before storage or AI use.

Assignment/header/credential-URL, private-key/token and conservative entropy masking cover logs, audit, discovery metadata and AI context before storage/use. Sensitive runtime identities are refused; secret files/history remain excluded. Best-effort detection is not exhaustive.
Use Bitwarden CLI to check whether linked items still exist.

sections.title: Backup and restore
rows: Back up selected configuration, data directories, and volumes.
Locally approved restic profiles select one to eight config/data/mounted-volume directories; fixed argv, immutable snapshots and signed durable intents. No automatic volume export.
Store backups on the configured NAS through an SMB/NFS mount.
Existing owner-mounted SMB/NFS storage and provisioned repository required; missing mount or changed mount identity refuses local fallback. Actual NAS permissions and restore remain unverified.
Run on demand, daily, or weekly.
Confirmed manual and opt-in daily/weekly UTC backups with durable once-only windows, no restart backlog or automatic retries. Demo automatic dispatch is disabled.
Configure snapshot retention, such as seven daily and four weekly backups.
Bounded daily/weekly policy, dry-run removal review and separately approved exact-ID forget; safety snapshots excluded. No automatic prune or deletion.
Stop-copy-start for consistency, or live copying for static configuration.

Explicit static-file live profiles or observed stop-copy-start for independent runtimes with stopped dependents; linked applications support static backups only. Uncertain outcomes retain a host hold.
Use restic repositories for encrypted, deduplicated backups.
Delegated to restic repositories; disposable real encrypted repository backup/restore/check verified locally. Native NAS and application acceptance remains pending.
Keep the repository password in Vaultwarden and supply it to the agent at runtime.
Owner supplies the vault-managed password through an approved PSC_ environment reference. Values never enter argv, registry or results; automatic vault login/unlock is excluded.
Include service-card exports and Compose/unit files.
Service-card Markdown shares the data snapshot; approved roots include Compose/unit files. Restored prose is returned for separate review without overwriting owner notes.
Show last success, size, next run, and failures.
Per-service history includes last success, snapshot IDs, byte counts, next UTC window and failures/unknown holds; policy alone never implies backup availability.
Choose a backup and inspect files before restoring.
Full immutable scoped snapshot selection, bounded file metadata preview, traversal/link/special-file refusal and separate overwrite confirmation.
Stop the service, restore files, start it, and run a health check.

Independent runtime stop, staged verified restore, atomic file overlay, restart if originally running and configured health check. Previously stopped runtimes remain stopped with health unverified; extra current files are preserved.
Capture current data before overwriting it.

Mandatory completed current-data snapshot before target overwrites, durable safety ID before overlay, native metadata checks and interrupted-operation inspection. No multi-file transaction or automatic rollback is claimed.
Backup/restore failures feed the existing masked notification outbox and persistent audit/history; real external delivery remains deployment verification.

sections.title: Unknown-activity and malware-related ideas
rows: Flag activity not previously recorded or approved.
Flag new systemd units, cron jobs, containers, and listening ports.

Reviewed unit/container discovery plus opt-in cron file/job, Windows Run/RunOnce and TCP-listener metadata diffs with explicit baseline acknowledgment, stale fingerprints and incomplete-provider safeguards; no commands or permissions are changed.
Watch changes to shell startup files, autostart entries, SSH authorized keys, and systemd configuration.
Flag processes executing from /tmp, /dev/shm, or deleted binaries.
Run external scanners periodically through agents.
Present scan findings on the host page.

sections.title: Security, platform support, and future extensions
rows: Bind to Tailscale and avoid public internet exposure.

Standard CLI listeners require loopback or an IP verified against the running local Tailscale identity. Compose explicitly permits its internal listener while publishing the host port on loopback. Private ingress/ACL deployment remains owner setup; no network changes were applied.
Passkey or password plus TOTP. The earlier chat suggested initially skipping application authentication; the spec adds it.

Optional single-owner scrypt password plus six-digit TOTP, replay/rate limits, revocable 12-hour HttpOnly/SameSite sessions, HTTPS for remote login, logout and configuration-change revocation; API bearer access remains available.
Controller authentication through mTLS certificates or signed tokens/commands.

Bearer tokens plus opt-in independent HMAC request signatures covering method/target/body/time/nonce; durable nonce claims reject replays across restart. Persistent channels additionally prove both endpoints and sign each sequence-bound frame. mTLS is an alternative, not implemented.
Allow-listed runtime actions and narrowly scoped privileged operations.

Runtime/profile/file allow-lists, non-root startup and a narrow exact-unit/action polkit template exist. Actual journal, Docker and unit privilege grants need reviewed target-host setup and verification; no broad runtime groups are granted by the installer.
Restrict declared paths and reject traversal/symlink escapes.
Approved-root checks, traversal rejection, resolved symlink escape checks and blocked secret-file previews.
Log control actions, restores, reverts, shutdowns, and shell sessions.

Durable authenticated write intents plus semantic controls, backup/restore/retention, inspection and schedule records; interrupted results remain unknown and are never replayed. Bodies and secrets are excluded.
Ubuntu and CachyOS, including relevant package-manager and shell differences.

Ubuntu/Debian/CachyOS/Arch installer prerequisites, systemd/shared runtime adapters, dpkg/pacman/RPM and desktop inventory are implemented in source. Actual Ubuntu/CachyOS installation, permissions and CLI behavior remain unverified.
Support Pi and x86 hosts; target approximately 250 MB combined controller/agent RAM.
Portable source and build definitions exist; Docker is unavailable here. Both-target image builds and the approximately 250 MB Pi controller/agent memory target remain unverified.
Compose deployment for the controller; agent installer and systemd service.

Controller Compose/Dockerfile and reviewed Ubuntu/Debian/CachyOS/Arch agent installer with a default plan and explicit apply, non-root account, private state, preserved existing files and hardened systemd unit. Installer syntax verified; no target installation, service activation or image build was executed.
REST operations plus WebSocket state, logs, and terminal streams.
REST, authenticated state/event/log streams and interactive terminal WebSockets; one-use owner-bound attach tickets, signed agent requests, host reservations, bounded streams and disconnect cleanup.
Native-style mobile push through the PWA.
Let Claude or a local LLM query and control services.
Visualize dependencies and the impact of stopping a service.

Notebook graph and full linked lists show recorded prerequisites and transitive dependents/stop impact, observed states, bounded diagram nodes and unknown references. It does not infer undeclared dependencies or execute controls.
Snapshot before image updates and automatically roll back if health checks fail.
A possible Zero 2 W for power cycling or serial-console access when another host is unreachable.

sections.title: Expanded scope and current additions
rows: CPU, memory, disk, network, temperatures and system history.

Native telemetry, volume/interface views, reset-aware disk/network rates and charts, sustained threshold policy/state and monitoring links exist. Optional adapters and measured Pi collection/resource budget remain.
Container inventory and individual control/log access.
Dedicated persistent container screen, Compose components, current-state checks, confirmed allow-listed controls, filtered logs and snapshot downloads.
Validated preview/import/export and repeat-import reconciliation are implemented.
Browse templates and install supported applications.
Cluster workload inventory, health, logs and lifecycle controls.
Nodes, guests, resource details and power controls.
Services, processes, ports, telemetry, Event Logs and dual-boot identity.

Read-only Windows services/apps/processes/TCP/UDP/Event Log inventory, section-level availability/staleness, optional physical-host identity and OS-switch access invalidation are implemented. Providers are mocked; real dual-boot deployment is unverified.
Linked Markdown vault export and conflict-aware owner-note sync.
Manual linked-vault export/sync works; automatic watching and remote sharing are future extensions.
A personalized paper cover on every service notebook.
Each banner uses its service name, host, runtime and note excerpt.
Theme covers dashboard, notebook banners, forms and dialogs; preference persists across reloads.
Accent color, density, text size and reduced motion.
Saved per browser, with reset and cross-tab preference synchronization.
Detect installed software including AutoCAD and Microsoft products and open recommended help/removal pages.

Read-only machine/agent-user uninstall registry and optional current-user Store inventory with curated official Autodesk/Microsoft/Office/Edge links. No uninstall strings, downloads or uninstall execution.
Include Linux and macOS software, process and socket visibility with appropriate official documentation and removal guidance.

Bounded read-only dpkg/pacman/RPM and desktop-entry inventory, standard macOS app bundles, agent-account process/socket metadata, curated OS-specific links, physical identity/OS-switch checks and scoped synthetic examples. Flatpak/Snap/AppImage/Homebrew/receipts and other users are excluded.
Focus on macOS alongside Linux and Windows.

Current-context inventory plus explicitly approved ordinary-user GUI LaunchAgent start/stop/restart with domain/path/hash and fresh-state guards, and mocked ACL/xattr editing. Actual old-macOS compatibility, launchctl context/output, permissions and Intel/Apple Silicon deployment remain unverified; system/Apple jobs remain read-only.
